children: has decided not to proceed with its planned acquisition of F9 Brands after determining F9 was unable to satisfy all closing requirements within the expected timeframe. In addition, Neighborhood will not enter into a commercial or strategic collaboration with F9. Going forward, the companies will continue to operate independently, and the terms and economics of the previously announced acquisition agreement are no longer in effect.No shares will be issued, and no acquisition capital will be deployed in connection with the proposed F9 transaction. As of August 31, after giving effect to the completed acquisitions of The Container Store, Kirkland’s, Installed Right, and SFV Construction Services, Neighborhood had approximately 97M shares of common stock issued and outstanding."Disciplined capital allocation and protecting shareholder value are central to how we evaluate every transaction," stated CEO Marcus Lemonis. "We evaluate opportunities continuously, and this is one of many transactions we have considered that we elected not to pursue. In this case, we determined the seller was unable to satisfy the closing conditions, which are essential to our confidence in any business we acquire," he added.Looking ahead, the company plans to remain focused on the strength of the Home Services platform, anchored by Elfa, Closet Works, and SFV Construction Services, and on pursuing opportunities that meet its strategic, financial, and operational standards.

title: Neighborhood Intelligence moves away from proposed F9 acquisition
